To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MLfBM estimator is the best in terms of accuracy and robustness, and it is the only estimator that can provide an estimate of the confidence interval for the rotation-scaling-rotation transformation vector.

the proposed MLfBm method outperforms other state-of-the art methods for subpixel registration in the presence of rotation, scaling, and translation transformations, and that this performance improvement can be quantified using a Cramér–Rao lower bound on the estimation error.

the maximum-likelihood estimator of the rotation-scaling-rotation transformation vector based on the fractal image model (MLfBm) is more accurate than any other estimator of this vector and that the accuracy of this estimator can be predicted by the Cramé-Rao lower bound on parameter estimation error, which depends on texture rough-ness, noise level, correlation between reference and template images and on transformation parameters.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MLf Bm estimator is more accurate than the state-of-the-art estimators for a large class of images and it is the best choice for the registration of images with high correlation.

the proposed method is a robust and efficient tool for area-based subpixel rotation-scaling- and translation-based registration of images with isotropic normally distributed texture and stationary increments.

the proposed method provides the best accuracy of the transformation vector estimation among other state-of-the- art methods, and it is also the most accurate method in the case when a priori information about the image texture is available.

the proposed approach is more accurate and robust to noise than the state-of-the-art techniques.
